deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck compares two kinds of structure.
- 2-dimensional arrangements: finite families of pseudolines in the real projective plane, viewed as cell decompositions of RP^2, with isomorphisms forming a groupoid.
- '1-dimensional arrangements': only the 1-skeleton data. This means the index set I of pseudolines, the set of vertices (intersection points, possibly multiple), and for each pseudoline the cyclic order of the vertices on it, i.e. the graph or 1-complex K_I together with its decomposition into 'lines'.

There is an obvious forgetful functor from 2-dim to 1-dim arrangements. The hypothesis 'sans bigones' (no 2-gonal faces) excludes the degenerate pencil case: in a projective arrangement with at least 3 pseudolines, not all concurrent, every face is at least a triangle.

Previous page. Grothendieck works through the reconstruction of a 2-cell structure from 1-dim data, using sub-configurations K_{J'} of 6 pseudolines. Faces are recognised locally, and an orientation of each local triangle K_J must be prescribed consistently, independent of the auxiliary choice J'. He isolates one exceptional case where three 'supplementary' pseudolines are concurrent. This forces card I = 6 and the arrangement to be the complete quadrangle: 4 triple points, the 6 pseudolines joining them in pairs, and 3 extra double points (the diagonal points, where 'opposite' sides meet). The symmetry involved is the Klein four-group V_4.

This page, first part. It finishes the description of that exceptional case.
- a, b, c are the vertices of a triangle K_J.
- α, β, γ are the 'opposite' vertices, e.g. α = D_a ∩ (pseudoline through b and c), the diagonal points of the quadrangle.
- λ_a, λ_b, λ_c are the edges of K_I containing α, β, γ.
- One chooses among {λ_a, λ_b, λ_c} compatibly with the orientation.
The point is that even here the local orientation data can be read off from the 1-skeleton, so the 2-cells are recovered.

This page, the theorem ('En résumé'). The canonical functor from the groupoid of (2-dim) pseudoline arrangements without bigons to the groupoid of 1-dim pseudoline arrangements (without bigons) is fully faithful. Concretely:
- two such arrangements are isomorphic as cell complexes of RP^2 iff their 1-skeleta-with-lines are isomorphic;
- every isomorphism of 1-dim data comes from a unique cellular isomorphism;
- in particular, Aut of the arrangement equals Aut of its 1-dim combinatorics.

This page, remaining programme.
- Conditions (A1)–(A5), from earlier pages, give in principle a description of the essential image: which abstract 1-dim structures are realisable by pseudoline arrangements. They need to be simplified first.
- One should also impose 'la relation d'EP (23)', presumably an Euler–Poincaré relation V − E + F = χ(RP^2) = 1 numbered (23) earlier. He conjectures it is automatic, i.e. a consequence of (A1)–(A5).

Purpose. This is a reconstruction or 'anabelian-style' statement: the 2-dimensional topological object is recovered functorially from 1-dimensional combinatorial data.
errors: No outright error visible. Full faithfulness relies on the case analysis of the preceding pages (the 6-line sub-configurations and the exceptional complete-quadrangle case); this page only sketches the orientation choice in that case, so the proof as written is a sketch.
The essential image is left uncharacterised. The claim that the Euler–Poincaré relation (23) follows automatically from (A1)–(A5) is stated as a supposition, not proved.

ideas.what: An arrangement of pseudolines (as a cell complex of RP^2, without digons) is determined, with its automorphisms, by its 1-dimensional data (vertices and their orders along each pseudoline): fully faithful forgetful functor between groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of pseudoline arrangements from local sequences / from the arrangement graph with line structure; combinatorial equivalence of arrangements and rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Felsner (local sequences determine simple arrangements, 1990s); Folkman–Lawrence 1978 (topological representation); Grünbaum 1972

ideas.what: Analysis of the exceptional configuration (complete quadrangle: 6 pseudolines, 4 triple points, 3 diagonal points, V_4 symmetry) where local reconstruction of face orientations needs special treatment.
ideas.modern_name: Complete quadrilateral/quadrangle arrangement; orientation of triangles in pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (projective geometry); in arrangement theory folklore

ideas.what: Programme to characterise the essential image (realisable abstract 1-dim line systems) by axioms (A1)–(A5), plus an Euler–Poincaré relation conjectured to be automatic.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic characterisation of realisable local sequences / abstract pseudoline systems (cf. oriented matroid axioms, signotopes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Felsner–Weil (sweeps, signotopes, 2001); oriented matroid axiomatics (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence)

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open a simplified axiomatics (A1)–(A5) for the essential image, i.e. which abstract 1-dim pseudoline systems, including non-simple ones with multiple points, are realisable as cell decompositions of RP^2. He also conjectures that the Euler–Poincaré relation is a consequence of the other axioms.
missed.quote: Les conditions (A1) à (A5) donnent en principe une voie pour déterminer l'image essentielle — mais il faut ... simplifier les conditions en question. ... je suppose que cette dernière est automatique.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Characterisations of local sequences exist mainly for simple arrangements. A clean axiomatics for non-simple arrangements directly at the level of 1-skeleta, with Euler-relation redundancy, would be a modest addition, though largely subsumed by oriented matroid theory.

missed.claim: The theorem is stated in groupoid language: the forgetful functor is fully faithful, recovering automorphisms too. It covers arrangements without bigons, apparently including non-simple ones. This is an early (c. 1981) independent formulation of the reconstruction of arrangements from 1-dimensional combinatorics.
missed.quote: Le foncteur canonique du groupoïde des arrangements de pseudodroites sans bigones, vers des arrangements 1 dimensionnels de pseudo-droites (sans bigones) est pleinement fidèle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. The content is essentially known (local sequences / oriented matroids determine the arrangement), but the functorial, groupoid-based formulation including automorphisms is not standard in the arrangements literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, essentially correct result that is close to known facts: arrangements are determined by local sequences, and rank-3 oriented matroids are equivalent to pseudoline arrangements. It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's independent, functorial treatment, but unlikely to surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'La fonction canonique' should read 'Le foncteur canonique' (fully faithful functor between groupoids).

In 'arrangements de {+cellules [?]+} [-pseudodroites-]', the word above the line is uncertain. The main reading 'arrangements de pseudodroites sans bigones' is what the image supports; 'pseudodroites' is only partly overwritten.
'mais il faut d' abord [?] ; simplifier' reads more plausibly as 'mais il faut d'abord aviser ; simplifier les conditions en question' (uncertain).
'dans {λa, λb, λc} et compatible avec l'orientation' is probably abbreviated 'et comp. avec l'orientation'.
'relation d'EP (23)': EP likely stands for Euler–Poincaré, with equation number (23).
